title: Quick Revision: Sound

table: Particles vibrate along the direction of the wave. Sound in air is longitudinal.
Regions of high / low pressure and density
Distance between two consecutive compressions (or rarefactions), in m
Number of oscillations per second, in hertz (Hz). T = 1/ν
Decided by **frequency**: higher frequency, higher pitch

box: **v = λν** · T = 1/ν · Echo: distance to the reflector = (v × t)/2
Audible range: 20 Hz to 20 kHz · Below 20 Hz: infrasound · Above 20 kHz: ultrasound

bullets: Sound needs a medium; it cannot travel through a vacuum.
Speed of sound: **solids > liquids > gases**. In air it is about 344 m/s at 22 °C, and it increases with temperature.
An echo is heard only if the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later, so the obstacle must be at least **17.2 m** away.
Reverberation (repeated reflections) is reduced in halls with soft, sound-absorbing materials on walls and seats.
Uses of ultrasound: detecting cracks in metal, cleaning hard-to-reach parts, scanning internal organs (ultrasonography), SONAR.
Forgetting to halve the distance in echo and SONAR questions (the sound goes there and back).
